title: Valid Sudoku
description:
# Valid Sudoku

Determine whether a partially filled `9 x 9` Sudoku board is valid. You only need to check cells that already contain a digit; empty cells are written as `'.'`.

A board is valid when all of these rules hold:

1. No row contains the same digit twice.
2. No column contains the same digit twice.
3. No `3 x 3` sub-box contains the same digit twice.

A valid board does not have to be solvable. This task only validates the digits that are already present.

The nine boxes are fixed: combine row groups 1–3, 4–6, 7–9 with the same three column groups to form nine disjoint `3 x 3` boxes.

## Example 1:

**Input:** board =
[["5","3",".",".","7",".",".",".","."],
 ["6",".",".","1","9","5",".",".","."],
 [".","9","8",".",".",".",".","6","."],
 ["8",".",".",".","6",".",".",".","3"],
 ["4",".",".","8",".","3",".",".","1"],
 ["7",".",".",".","2",".",".",".","6"],
 [".","6",".",".",".",".","2","8","."],
 [".",".",".","4","1","9",".",".","5"],
 [".",".",".",".","8",".",".","7","9"]]
**Output:** true

## Example 2:

**Input:** board =
[["8","3",".",".","7",".",".",".","."],
 ["6",".",".","1","9","5",".",".","."],
 [".","9","8",".",".",".",".","6","."],
 ["8",".",".",".","6",".",".",".","3"],
 ["4",".",".","8",".","3",".",".","1"],
 ["7",".",".",".","2",".",".",".","6"],
 [".","6",".",".",".",".","2","8","."],
 [".",".",".","4","1","9",".",".","5"],
 [".",".",".",".","8",".",".","7","9"]]
**Output:** false
**Explanation:** The digit `8` appears twice in column `0`.

## Constraints:

*   `board.length == 9`
*   `board[i].length == 9`
*   `board[i][j]` is a digit `1-9` or `'.'`.

tests.description: Column conflict: 8 appears twice in column 0
Sub-box conflict: 1 appears twice in top-left 3x3 box

solutions.name: HashSet for Each Row, Column, Box
solutions.description:
## Approach

Maintain separate sets for the 9 rows, 9 columns, and 9 sub-boxes. When a filled cell is visited, check whether its digit has already appeared in the corresponding row, column, or box. The 3x3 box index is `(row / 3) * 3 + (col / 3)`.

## Key Insight

A partially filled Sudoku board is valid if and only if every filled digit is unique within all three constraint groups. Empty cells are ignored; the task is not to solve the board.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(81) = O(1)
- Space Complexity: O(81) = O(1)

solutions.name: Single HashSet with Encoding
solutions.description:
## Approach

Use one set of encoded strings. For a digit `d` at `(row, col)`, insert three records: `d` in this row, `d` in this column, and `d` in this box. If any insert fails because the record already exists, the board is invalid.

## Key Insight

The encoded-set approach collapses three separate collections into one uniform membership check. It is concise and makes every Sudoku constraint look like the same duplicate-detection problem.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(81) = O(1)
- Space Complexity: O(81) = O(1)

solutions.name: Bit Manipulation
solutions.description:
## Approach

Represent each row, column, and box as a bit mask. Digit `d` corresponds to bit `d`. For each filled cell, test whether that bit is already set in any of the three masks; if not, set it.

## Key Insight

Bit masks are a compact version of the set approach. They are useful because Sudoku digits are limited to 1 through 9, so all membership information fits inside a small integer.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(81) = O(1)
- Space Complexity: O(27) = O(1)
